messages:
Aisha (AE): CedarTrust confirmed they want to run a 5-day POC next week. They require Private/VPC connectivity, perimeter TLS inspection, and an allowlist for security. Qs for us: 1) Can PrivateLink play nice with their DPI? 2) Can we provide a single static egress IP for their firewall? 3) Short firewall snippet + 2-line security blurb for their packet. @Tom @Raj @Priya please.

Tom (Solutions): TL;DR: Yes, but with two recommended patterns.
Pattern A - PrivateLink (interface endpoint) only: keeps traffic off public internet from customer side. Customers DPI must not break mutual auth; if they terminate TLS, cert-based auth may break. This is lowest ops on our side.
Pattern B - Connector in-customer-VPC: we deploy a lightweight connector (container/VM) in their subnet that forwards requests to Redwood. This preserves client IP visibility and lets customer run DPI locally before traffic leaves their network.

Tom (Solutions): Static egress IPs: we can provide an HA pair (two /32s) as a managed add-on for Private deployments. For the POC we can reserve one IP as a temporary allowlist entry. Will need approval from Finance for pricing.

Raj (NetOps): Minimal firewall snippet for their packet (pasteable):
```
# CedarTrust POC - Redwood allowlist (example)
# Replace <REDFW_EGRESS> and <PRIVLINK_ENI_CIDR> with values we provide

# Allow interface endpoint traffic (PrivateLink ENIs in customer subnets)
ALLOW tcp from <customer_app_subnets> to <PRIVLINK_ENI_CIDR> port 443

# Allow outbound from connector or ENIs to Redwood egress
ALLOW tcp from <connector_or_enis> to <REDFW_EGRESS> ports 443

# Health/DNS/NTP
ALLOW udp from <connector_or_enis> to 8.8.8.8 port 53
ALLOW udp from <connector_or_enis> to <NTP_POOL> port 123
```

Raj (NetOps): Notes: PrivateLink creates ENIs in their subnets. Those ENIs are local IPs they can control security for. Our backend connections will originate from Redwood-managed egress IP(s). If they need full TLS visibility for auditing, recommend the connector pattern. Also confirm whether they expect client IP preservation for logs (connector preserves it).

Priya (Security): Security blurb for their packet (2 lines):
"Redwood will deploy an interface endpoint into customer-managed subnets. Outbound model requests initiated from the endpoint will egress from Redwood-managed static IP(s) provided for the POC; if CedarTrust performs TLS inspection that terminates TLS, Redwood recommends either a connector deployment inside the VPC or a documented cert re-issue flow to preserve mutual-auth and auditability."

Priya (Security): Other bullets to include in questionnaire:
- TLS: TLS 1.2+ required; mTLS available for connector deployments.
- Data handling: By default, request payloads are not persisted beyond transient logs unless explicitly enabled; retention/export options can be contractually defined.

Tom (Solutions): Quick pricing sketch (POC packet):
- Single temporary static egress IP (POC) = $1,800/month (pro-rated)
- Connector deployment (small VM) = $450/month + $1,000 one-time setup (estimate)
- Dedicated reserved capacity for heavy throughput or lots of static IPs = starts at ~$18k/month (depends on size)
Numbers are estimates; Ill follow up with formal quote by COB Tue.

Aisha (AE): Thanks. Action items: Tom to confirm the actual IP(s) and firm quote by Tue COB. Raj to attach a one-page network sketch and list minimal subnet sizes (by Mon). Priya to add the security blurb into the questionnaire doc. I'll coordinate kickoff with CedarTrust. deploy-bot: New ticket created: POC-741 (CedarTrust - PrivateLink POC). :white_check_mark:

Tom (Solutions): Acknowledged, on it.

Raj (NetOps): Acknowledged  will share sketch and ENI CIDR guidance.

Aisha (AE): Thanks team, I'll update CedarTrust and schedule the initial call.
